options.B: Ensuring continuity of medical follow-up
options.C: Providing access to professional social workers
options.D: Connecting the client with community support groups

explanation: Good referral networks are designed to build a strong safety net and reduce isolation, never to cut a client off from the people who love and support them. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h7)

question: What is the maximum gestational age used to define an abortion?

options.A: Before 20 weeks of gestation
options.B: Before 37 weeks of gestation
options.C: Before 28 weeks of gestation
options.D: Before 12 weeks of gestation

explanation: An abortion is classified as the loss of a pregnancy before 20 weeks of gestation, or when the baby weighs less than 500 grams. You've got this!

question: A patient has vaginal bleeding, mild lower tummy cramps, but her cervix is still tightly closed. What kind of abortion is this?

options.A: Incomplete abortion
options.B: Threatened abortion
options.C: Inevitable abortion
options.D: Complete abortion

explanation: When bleeding and cramps happen but the cervix stays closed, it's called a threatened abortion because the pregnancy might still continue safely.

question: Which test is best for checking if any pregnancy tissue is left inside the uterus?

options.A: Urinalysis dipstick
options.B: Endometrial biopsy
options.C: Abdominal X-ray
options.D: Pelvic ultrasound

explanation: A pelvic ultrasound gives a clear picture of the inside of the uterus so we can easily tell if it's completely empty or if tissue remains.

question: Why do we check the Rhesus blood group for a patient having an incomplete abortion?

options.A: To calculate her exact gestational age
options.B: To check for severe iron deficiency anemia
options.C: To find out if she has a bacterial infection
options.D: To see if she needs anti-D immunoglobulin

explanation: If a mother is Rhesus-negative, giving anti-D immunoglobulin protects her future pregnancies from blood-type mismatch issues. Great clinical thinking!

question: What is the first life-saving goal when treating a patient with heavy bleeding from an abortion?

options.A: Discharging the patient home with pain relief
options.B: Restoring circulating blood volume and perfusion
options.C: Conducting a detailed psychosocial interview
options.D: Scheduling routine laboratory blood tests

explanation: When there is heavy bleeding, stopping shock and getting fluids back into circulation is always the number one emergency priority.

question: Why is a urinary catheter put in place when treating a patient in severe shock from bleeding?

options.A: To stop the patient from moving around in bed
options.B: To empty the bladder before a surgical procedure
options.C: To collect a clean-catch urine culture specimen
options.D: To monitor hourly urine output to check kidney function

explanation: Urine output is a fantastic mirror for how well the kidneys and vital organs are receiving blood during resuscitation.

question: Which medication is used in medical abortion to cause strong uterine contractions?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Ergometrine
options.C: Misoprostol
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Misoprostol helps the uterus contract and safely push out any remaining tissue. You'll see this drug used a lot in ward practice!

question: What does mifepristone do when used in a medical abortion?

options.A: Blocks progesterone to soften the cervix and break down the lining
options.B: Stops sudden bacterial growth inside the womb
options.C: Lowers blood pressure during heavy bleeding
options.D: Provides immediate pain relief from cramps

explanation: Mifepristone prepares the ground by blocking progesterone, making the follow-up medication (misoprostol) work smoothly.

question: What is the preferred gentle way to clear the uterus in an early pregnancy loss up to 14 weeks?

options.A: Diagnostic laparoscopy
options.B: Manual Vacuum Aspiration
options.C: Cesarean section delivery
options.D: Total abdominal hysterectomy

explanation: Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) is safe, quick, and very effective for early evacuation with fewer complications.

question: What important task must a nurse do right after a surgical uterine evacuation?

options.A: Perform a pelvic exam without gloves
options.B: Discharge the patient home right away
options.C: Administer general anesthesia
options.D: Inspect the removed tissue to confirm everything came out

explanation: Always check the evacuated tissue! It guarantees no tissue was left behind, keeping the patient safe from infection.

question: How soon can a woman start ovulating again after having an abortion?

options.A: After six months
options.B: After three menstrual cycles
options.C: Within two weeks
options.D: After one year

explanation: Fertility can bounce back as early as two weeks! That's why family planning counseling before discharge is super important.

question: Why is Post-Abortion Care (PAC) considered a complete, all-round care model?

options.A: It involves police reports for every single case
options.B: It delays discharge until lab results are ready
options.C: It combines emergency treatment, family planning, and emotional support
options.D: It focuses only on theatre surgeries

explanation: PAC looks at the whole patient—healing her body, supporting her emotions, and helping her plan for the future.

question: Which of these is NOT a direct complication of an unsafe or incomplete abortion?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Intrauterine adhesions
options.C: Severe pelvic infection
options.D: Heavy hemorrhage

explanation: Gestational diabetes is linked to metabolic changes during an ongoing pregnancy, whereas bleeding, infection, and adhesions follow abortion complications.

question: A patient returns three days after an abortion with fever, lower tummy pain, and a bad-smelling discharge. What does this point to?

options.A: Complete abortion
options.B: Normal recovery phase
options.C: Ectopic pregnancy
options.D: Septic abortion

explanation: Fever, pain, and foul discharge are classic warning signs of a septic abortion needing quick antibiotics. You'll spot these clinical cues easily in the ward!

question: Under Nigerian law, when is an abortion legally allowed?

options.A: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.B: When the pregnancy is a result of rape
options.C: When there is severe financial hardship
options.D: Whenever the woman requests it

explanation: Nigerian law permits termination only when it is strictly necessary to save the mother's life.

question: What is your main duty as a nurse when a patient comes in with complications from an illegal abortion?

options.A: Report her to security before starting any fluids
options.B: Lecture her on the morality of her actions
options.C: Provide immediate, non-judgmental life-saving emergency care
options.D: Refuse treatment until the police arrive

explanation: As a professional nurse, saving a life always comes first. We treat every patient with care, empathy, and zero judgment.

question: What is the key difference between a spontaneous abortion and an induced abortion?

options.A: Spontaneous abortions happen naturally, while induced abortions are deliberately brought about.
options.B: Induced abortions occur due to chromosomal issues, while spontaneous abortions involve trauma.
options.C: Induced abortions only occur in the first trimester, while spontaneous abortions occur later.
options.D: Spontaneous abortions always require surgery, while induced abortions use only medication.

explanation: You've got this! A spontaneous abortion is a natural loss of pregnancy (often called a miscarriage), whereas an induced abortion is deliberately done using medical or surgical methods.

question: When do immediate complications of an abortion typically show up?

options.A: Between one and two weeks after the event
options.B: During the procedure or within the first 24 hours
options.C: Only after a subsequent pregnancy begins
options.D: Several months to years later

explanation: Think of 'immediate' as happening right away! These complications usually show up while the procedure is going on or within the first 24 hours.

question: What is the most frequent cause of heavy bleeding after an abortion?

options.A: Severe high blood pressure
options.B: An allergic reaction to antibiotics
options.C: Retained products of conception
options.D: A sudden drop in body temperature

explanation: When tiny bits of tissue are left behind in the uterus, the muscle cannot clamp down tight to stop the bleeding. Always suspect retained tissue when heavy bleeding happens!

question: A patient after an abortion has a weak, fast pulse, low blood pressure, and cold skin. What condition is she likely developing?

options.A: Uterine perforation
options.B: Hypovolemic shock
options.C: Postpartum depression
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Spotting these vital signs is a core nursing skill! A fast pulse, low BP, and cold skin tell us the body is running low on fluid volume due to heavy bleeding—classic hypovolemic shock.

question: What happens during a uterine perforation?

options.A: An instrument punctures the wall of the uterus.
options.B: The uterine muscle permanently stops contracting.
options.C: Blood clots block the fallopian tubes completely.
options.D: The cervix fails to dilate during surgery.

explanation: Simply put, 'perforation' means a hole. It occurs when a surgical instrument accidentally pokes through the muscular wall of the uterus.

question: Which of these is NOT a sign that a uterine perforation might have happened?

options.A: Sudden relief from all abdominal cramping
options.B: Tenderness across the lower abdomen
options.C: Severe and worsening lower abdominal pain
options.D: Signs of internal bleeding and low blood pressure

explanation: A perforated uterus causes worsening pain and tenderness—not sudden relief! Always watch out for sharp abdominal pain after instrumentation.

question: What is endometritis?

options.A: A blood clot inside the deep veins of the leg
options.B: A complete tear in the muscular wall of the bladder
options.C: An allergic reaction to surgical anesthesia
options.D: An infection of the inner lining of the uterus

explanation: Look at the root words: 'endometrio' refers to the inner lining of the uterus, and '-itis' means inflammation or infection. You've got this!

question: Why does leftover tissue inside the uterus sharply increase the risk of infection?

options.A: It lowers the body temperature below normal levels.
options.B: It stops the liver from producing infection-fighting proteins.
options.C: It provides an ideal environment for bacteria to multiply.
options.D: It directly inactivates all circulating white blood cells.

explanation: Bacteria love stagnant, dead tissue mixed with blood! Leftover tissue creates a cozy breeding ground where bacteria can easily multiply and cause infection.

question: What is Asherman's syndrome?

options.A: A chronic bacterial infection of the fallopian tubes
options.B: The formation of scar tissue inside the uterine cavity
options.C: The complete inability of the cervix to ever dilate
options.D: Permanent high blood pressure following heavy bleeding

explanation: Asherman's syndrome happens when scar tissue (adhesions) forms inside the uterus, which can sometimes interfere with future periods or fertility.

question: How can a prior traumatic abortion affect a woman's future pregnancies?

options.A: It permanently prevents the placenta from attaching anywhere in the body.
options.B: It guarantees that all future babies will develop chromosomal disorders.
options.C: It can cause cervical incompetence, increasing the risk of premature birth.
options.D: It stops the mother's body from producing breast milk later.

explanation: If the cervix is injured or stretched too forcefully during a procedure, its muscles may become weak. This weakness (cervical incompetence) makes it harder for the cervix to stay closed during a later pregnancy.

question: What is the main reason for doing a pelvic ultrasound when post-abortion complications are suspected?

options.A: To determine the patient's exact psychological state
options.B: To check for retained products of conception or free fluid
options.C: To test for specific bacterial strains causing infection
options.D: To measure the patient's exact blood clotting time

explanation: An ultrasound gives doctors a clear 'window' inside to check if any pregnancy tissue was left behind or if fluid leaked where it shouldn't.

question: A patient reports soaking three large sanitary pads in less than an hour after an abortion. What should you as a nurse do first?

options.A: Discharge the patient home with instructions to return in one week.
options.B: Advise the patient to take a hot bath and rest in bed.
options.C: Report the heavy bleeding to the clinician and assess vital signs.
options.D: Tell the patient this is a completely normal post-procedure finding.

explanation: Soaking more than two pads an hour is a red flag for hemorrhage! Your immediate nursing priority is to check her vital signs and notify the doctor right away.

question: What is the primary power source for creating a vacuum during an MVA procedure?

options.A: A wall-mounted hospital vacuum pipeline
options.B: A foot-pumped mechanical pressure valve
options.C: A manually operated hand-held syringe
options.D: A heavy-duty electric suction machine

explanation: An MVA relies entirely on a hand-held syringe that the operator pulls to generate a vacuum, eliminating the need for electricity. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h1)

question: Up to what gestational age is MVA typically performed in the first trimester?

options.A: 28 to 30 weeks
options.B: 12 to 14 weeks
options.C: 4 to 6 weeks
options.D: 20 to 22 weeks

explanation: MVA is designed and validated as a safe and effective procedure for early pregnancy loss and termination up to 12 to 14 weeks of gestation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT an indication for manual vacuum aspiration?

options.A: Endometrial biopsy for abnormal uterine bleeding
options.B: Management of a full-term normal vaginal delivery
options.C: First-trimester elective termination of pregnancy
options.D: Incomplete miscarriage with retained tissue

explanation: MVA is restricted to first-trimester uterine evacuation and diagnostic sampling, not full-term deliveries. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h2)

question: Why is active pelvic inflammatory disease considered a strong contraindication for immediate MVA?

options.A: It stops the vacuum syringe from creating negative pressure
options.B: It turns the remaining tissue into hard calcified masses
options.C: It makes the uterine muscle completely resistant to dilation
options.D: It can spread infection upward into the pelvic cavity

explanation: Entering an infected uterus with surgical instruments risks pushing bacteria further into the upper reproductive tract, worsening sepsis or pelvic infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h2)

question: What is the function of the flexible plastic canulas used in an MVA kit?

options.A: To seal the outside opening of the vagina during suction
options.B: To travel through the cervix and vacuum out uterine tissue
options.C: To measure the exact internal temperature of the uterus
options.D: To pump local anesthetic pain medicine into the cervix

explanation: Canulas are the sterile tubes inserted past the cervix into the uterus to channel the suctioned tissue into the syringe. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h3)

question: What must the nurse check or do immediately before pulling back the syringe plunger to create a vacuum?

options.A: Boil the entire plastic syringe in hot water
options.B: Attach a heavy electrical cord to the back handle
options.C: Ensure the vacuum valves or buttons are closed
options.D: Fill the cylinder completely with sterile water

explanation: If the valves are left open while pulling the plunger, air simply enters the syringe from the outside and no vacuum is created. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h3)

question: Why is it important for a patient to empty her bladder right before an MVA procedure?

options.A: To stop the kidneys from producing urine for the next several hours
options.B: To prevent accidental urine contamination of the surgical field
options.C: To test kidney function before giving any local anesthetic drugs
options.D: To make the pelvic exam and uterine positioning easier and less painful

explanation: A full bladder displaces the uterus, makes bimanual palpation difficult, and increases patient discomfort during speculum and instrument insertion. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h4)

question: A patient scheduled for MVA is visibly shaking and expresses fear of severe pain. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Sit close, explain the steps calmly, and offer emotional reassurance
options.B: Cancel the procedure immediately and reschedule for another day
options.C: Tell her that pain is minor and she should try to stay strong
options.D: Administer a strong general anesthetic drug without a doctor's order

explanation: Anxious patients benefit greatly from calm explanations, validation of their feelings, and reassurance, which helps reduce physical tension and perceived pain. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h4)

question: What clinical sign typically tells the clinician that the uterine cavity is successfully emptied during MVA?

options.A: The syringe plunger automatically pushes itself back
options.B: The patient falls into a deep sleep
options.C: Fluid turns completely clear without any blood bubbles
options.D: Bright red foam appears and a gritty feeling is sensed

explanation: When tissue is cleared, the canula comes into contact with the empty uterine wall, producing a characteristic gritty sound or feel along with red foam in the tubing. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h5)

question: What is the purpose of performing a bimanual examination right before an MVA starts?

options.A: To determine the exact size and position of the uterus
options.B: To scrape away loose tissue without needing a canula
options.C: To check if the patient's bladder is completely empty
options.D: To measure the patient's blood pressure and pulse rate

explanation: Knowing whether the uterus is tilted forward or backward helps the clinician guide instruments smoothly and prevents accidental perforation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h5)

question: How often should vital signs be monitored immediately after an MVA procedure during the first hour?

options.A: Only if the patient complains of dizziness
options.B: Every hour on the hour
options.C: Every 5 minutes
options.D: Every 15 minutes

explanation: Frequent checks every 15 minutes during the first hour help catch early signs of hemorrhage or vasovagal shock. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h6)

question: Which instruction should a nurse give a patient regarding pelvic rest after an MVA?

options.A: Avoid eating solid food for at least 48 hours post-procedure
options.B: Keep taking vaginal douches daily to clean out old blood
options.C: Exercise strenuously starting the very next morning
options.D: Avoid sexual intercourse and tampons for about two weeks

explanation: To prevent bacteria from entering the healing cervix and causing an infection, patients are advised against putting anything in the vagina for two weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h6)

question: What is the primary cause of a vasovagal reaction during cervical manipulation or MVA?

options.A: An acute drop in the patient's body temperature
options.B: Complete blockage of the airway by mucus
options.C: Sudden stimulation of nerves around the cervix
options.D: A severe allergic reaction to the plastic syringe

explanation: Stretching or manipulating the cervix triggers nerve responses that can lower the heart rate and blood pressure, causing fainting or dizziness. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h7)

question: A patient recovering from an MVA suddenly complains of dizziness, looks pale, and her pulse drops. What is the nurse's best immediate action?

options.A: Elevate the patient's legs and monitor vital signs
options.B: Take her to the operating room for an emergency laparotomy
options.C: Administer a strong dose of oral antibiotics
options.D: Tell her to stand up and walk around to improve circulation

explanation: Elevating the legs helps blood return to the brain during a vasovagal episode, quickly relieving dizziness and fainting symptoms. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h7)

question: What is the very first step required for MVA instruments immediately after a procedure is finished?

options.A: Placing them into a decontamination solution
options.B: Wrapping them tightly in sterile cloth drapes
options.C: Storing them directly in a warm drying cabinet
options.D: Scrubbing them with dry steel wool pads

explanation: Decontaminating instruments right after use inactivates infectious agents and prevents blood from drying on the plastic surfaces. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h8)

question: Why is it important to inspect MVA plastic syringes and canulas closely before sterilization?

options.A: To ensure the plastic has changed color indicating expiration
options.B: To check for cracks, scratches, or wear that could harbor bacteria
options.C: To verify the manufacturing country and brand name
options.D: To measure how much weight the plastic can hold under pressure

explanation: Damaged or cracked plastic instruments cannot maintain a proper vacuum and can trap microorganisms, leading to infection risks. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h8)

question: What is the main job of mifepristone during a medical abortion?

options.A: Stimulating strong uterine contractions
options.B: Inducing systemic maternal hypertension
options.C: Blocking progesterone receptors to detach the sac
options.D: Paralyzing the musculature of the cervix

explanation: You've got this! Mifepristone blocks progesterone, the hormone needed to maintain pregnancy. This causes the uterine lining to soften and detaches the sac, preparing the way for the next step.

question: Why is misoprostol taken after mifepristone instead of taking it first?

options.A: It softens the cervix before the mifepristone is absorbed.
options.B: It triggers contractions to expel tissue loosened by the first drug.
options.C: It prevents heavy bleeding from starting too early.
options.D: It neutralizes the extreme toxicity of the first drug.

explanation: Great thinking! Mifepristone loosens the pregnancy tissue first, so when misoprostol comes in to cause uterine contractions, it can easily push the tissue out.

question: Up to how many weeks of pregnancy can a standard medical abortion safely be done?

options.A: Up to 20 to 22 weeks
options.B: Anytime during the first trimester only
options.C: Up to 10 to 11 weeks
options.D: Strictly within the first 4 weeks

explanation: Spot on! Medical abortion is most effective and safest when used within the first 10 to 11 weeks of pregnancy.

question: A patient requesting a medical abortion is found to have an IUD in place. What needs to happen first?

options.A: The patient must be switched immediately to a surgical procedure.
options.B: The medications can be given safely around the IUD.
options.C: The IUD must be removed before starting the medications.
options.D: Progesterone supplements should be given to offset the IUD.

explanation: Well done! Any existing intrauterine device (IUD) needs to be removed before starting the regimen to lower the risk of severe infection and make sure the medication works properly.

question: Which test is crucial before giving medical abortion drugs to rule out a dangerous condition where the pregnancy implants outside the uterus?

options.A: An electrocardiogram
options.B: An ultrasound to check for ectopic pregnancy
options.C: A routine chest X-ray
options.D: A complete metabolic panel

explanation: You nailed it! An ultrasound is essential to confirm the pregnancy is inside the uterus, ruling out a risky ectopic pregnancy.

question: Why is it so important to counsel patients on what to expect physically before they take abortion medications at home?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of the hospital visit.
options.B: It legally waives the clinic from malpractice claims.
options.C: It prepares them for the expected severe cramps and heavy bleeding at home.
options.D: It prevents heavy bleeding from starting too early.

explanation: Exactly! Knowing what normal cramps and bleeding look like helps patients manage their symptoms calmly at home without unnecessary panic.

question: How is mifepristone normally given in a standard abortion protocol?

options.A: Orally as a single tablet
options.B: Vaginally as a suppository
options.C: Intravenously in a fast infusion
options.D: Directly into the uterine cavity

explanation: That's correct! Mifepristone is simply taken by mouth as a single 200 mg tablet to kick off the process.

question: What is the usual waiting time between taking mifepristone and taking misoprostol?

options.A: 5 to 7 days
options.B: 2 weeks
options.C: 24 to 48 hours
options.D: 1 to 2 hours

explanation: Spot on! Patients usually wait 24 to 48 hours after swallowing the mifepristone tablet before taking the misoprostol.

question: Which temporary side effect is very common after taking misoprostol?

options.A: Complete temporary paralysis
options.B: High blood pressure requiring medication
options.C: Chills and low-grade fever
options.D: Severe permanent hair loss

explanation: You got it! Misoprostol frequently causes mild, temporary side effects like chills, nausea, or a slight fever. They pass quickly!

question: A patient calls the clinic worried because she has heavy cramps and is passing large clots after taking misoprostol. As a nurse, how do you view this?

options.A: It means the entire treatment has completely failed.
options.B: It is the expected normal physical response to the drugs.
options.C: It indicates a dangerous uterine rupture.
options.D: It is a sign of a severe medication allergy.

explanation: Brilliant! Heavy cramping and passing clots show that the medication is working and the uterus is emptying as it should.

question: Which bleeding pattern is a serious warning sign (red flag) after a medical abortion?

options.A: Passing a single clot the size of a coin
options.B: Spotting that lasts for up to three weeks
options.C: Bleeding that stops completely after 24 hours
options.D: Soaking through two large pads per hour for two hours

explanation: You're doing great! Soaking through two large pads every hour for two hours straight is too much—it's a red flag that needs prompt medical evaluation.

question: A patient calls reporting a fever of 38.5°C and severe pelvic pain three days after a medical abortion. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: An ongoing uterine infection
options.B: An allergic reaction to ibuprofen
options.C: A normal side effect of mifepristone
options.D: A normal reaction to lingering hormones

explanation: Spot on! A lingering fever and severe pain days after the procedure can signal a uterine infection that needs a doctor's attention and antibiotics.

question: When can a patient safely start a new method of contraception after a medical abortion?

options.A: Only after waiting six full months
options.B: After the next normal menstrual period
options.C: Immediately on the same day
options.D: Strictly after a surgical checkup

explanation: Correct! Fertility can return almost immediately, so patients can start new birth control methods like pills or implants on the exact same day they take the abortion medications.

question: Why is talking about birth control options right after a medical abortion so important?

options.A: It stops abnormal uterine bleeding from starting.
options.B: It helps prevent rapid repeat unintended pregnancies.
options.C: It prevents the uterus from contracting too forcefully.
options.D: It ensures that fertility returns safely after six months.

explanation: You nailed it! Because ovulation can happen as early as two weeks after an abortion, discussing contraception early helps patients avoid unplanned pregnancies before they are ready.

question: What is the main action of mifepristone in the body?

options.A: It prevents infection by suppressing the immune system
options.B: It stimulates strong, rhythmic uterine contractions
options.C: It directly softens the cervix by increasing estrogen
options.D: It acts as a progesterone receptor antagonist

explanation: You've got this! Mifepristone blocks progesterone, the key hormone that keeps the uterine lining thick and secure during pregnancy.

question: Why are two different medications used together in a medical abortion?

options.A: Combining them achieves a higher success rate than using either drug by itself
options.B: Using both drugs simultaneously shortens the bleeding duration by half
options.C: The second drug is needed immediately to reverse the side effects of the first
options.D: Mifepristone causes the contractions while misoprostol blocks the hormones

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Using mifepristone first to prepare the uterus and then misoprostol to empty it works best together for a complete process.

question: What is the specific job of misoprostol during a medical abortion?

options.A: It blocks the action of progesterone in the uterine lining
options.B: It causes uterine contractions to expel the pregnancy tissue
options.C: It prevents nausea caused by the breakdown of the decidua
options.D: It stops heavy bleeding by constricting pelvic blood vessels

explanation: Great job! Misoprostol is a prostaglandin that tells the smooth muscles of the uterus to contract and gently push out the tissue.

question: What happens in the uterus right after a patient takes mifepristone?

options.A: Muscles relax completely to prevent any early spotting
options.B: The myometrium immediately begins violent cramping
options.C: The uterine lining breaks down and the cervix softens
options.D: Blood vessels expand to increase oxygen delivery to the fetus

explanation: Spot on! By blocking progesterone, mifepristone gets the uterus ready and softens the cervix before the second drug is even taken.

question: Which of these is an absolute 'no-go' (contraindication) for using mifepristone and misoprostol?

options.A: A gestational age of exactly four weeks
options.B: A previous uncomplicated vaginal delivery
options.C: A history of mild seasonal allergies
options.D: A confirmed or suspected ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Remember, medical abortion only works inside the uterus. If the pregnancy is outside the uterus (ectopic), these drugs won't work and it's a major emergency!

question: A patient requesting a medical abortion has an intrauterine device (IUD) in place. What needs to happen first?

options.A: The IUD must be removed before the medications are administered
options.B: The dose of misoprostol should be doubled to compensate for the IUD
options.C: The IUD should only be removed if heavy bleeding starts
options.D: The patient can take mifepristone while the IUD remains inside

explanation: Safety first! The IUD has to come out before starting to prevent heavy bleeding or nasty pelvic infections.

question: What is the usual time gap between taking mifepristone and misoprostol?

options.A: Exactly one week apart
options.B: 24 to 48 hours
options.C: Immediately at the same time
options.D: 12 to 14 days apart

explanation: You'll often see 24 to 48 hours prescribed—this gives the first drug enough time to do its job so the second drug can work effectively.

question: Why is it important to talk about pain management before the patient takes misoprostol?

options.A: Pain medications must be taken to prevent allergic reactions to the drug
options.B: Analgesics speed up the absorption of the hormone in the stomach lining
options.C: Misoprostol causes strong uterine contractions that lead to significant cramping
options.D: Pain medication stops the excessive bleeding that occurs right away

explanation: Cramping is a very normal part of the process because the uterus is working hard to empty. Planning ahead for pain relief keeps our patients comfortable!

question: Which symptom is completely normal and expected after taking misoprostol?

options.A: Permanent cessation of all menstrual cycles
options.B: Immediate high fever lasting for several days
options.C: Temporary nausea, chills, or mild diarrhea
options.D: Complete numbness in the lower extremities

explanation: Don't panic if a patient experiences mild chills or tummy upset—these are common side effects of misoprostol that pass quickly.

question: What should a nurse tell a patient to expect regarding bleeding after taking these medications?

options.A: Expect bleeding that is heavier than a normal menstrual period with some clots
options.B: Expect only light spotting that stops entirely within two hours
options.C: Expect continuous heavy hemorrhaging that requires immediate blood transfusion
options.D: Expect no bleeding until at least one week after taking misoprostol

explanation: Since the body is clearing out the uterine lining and tissue, heavier bleeding with a few clots is expected and part of the process.

question: A patient calls saying she has soaked through two large sanitary pads every hour for three hours straight. What's your advice as the nurse?

options.A: Wait another six hours because heavy bleeding is always normal
options.B: Take another dose of misoprostol to finish the process
options.C: Apply a hot water bottle to the abdomen and rest in bed
options.D: Seek immediate medical evaluation for excessive bleeding

explanation: Soaking two heavy pads an hour for two hours in a row is our red flag for hemorrhage. Time to get them seen right away!

question: Which of these is NOT a normal sign of recovery after a medical abortion?

options.A: Having light spotting that tapers off over a couple of weeks
options.B: Passing blood clots along with lower abdominal cramping
options.C: A persistent high fever starting several days after misoprostol
options.D: Experiencing mild nausea that goes away within twenty-four hours

explanation: A high fever is never normal—it's a warning sign of a potential infection that needs a doctor's attention right away.

question: When can a patient typically start a new method of birth control after a medical abortion?

options.A: Only after waiting for three full menstrual cycles
options.B: Before taking the initial dose of mifepristone
options.C: Six months after the procedure is completed
options.D: Immediately or at the follow-up visit

explanation: Fertility bounces back super fast! Most birth control methods can be started right away on the day the abortion process is complete.

question: Why is talking about birth control early in post-abortion care so crucial?

options.A: Birth control pills must be taken to prevent future ectopic pregnancies
options.B: Ovulation can return as early as two weeks after the procedure
options.C: Hormonal contraceptives are required to stop ongoing uterine bleeding
options.D: Patients lose natural fertility permanently after a medication abortion

explanation: A patient can actually get pregnant again before their next normal period even arrives, so early counseling is a lifesaver.

question: What is a primary ethical duty for a Nigerian nurse caring for a patient with abortion complications?

options.A: Refuse treatment immediately if personal beliefs conflict with the procedure
options.B: Delay medical intervention until family members arrive to give consent
options.C: Report the patient to local law enforcement before providing aid
options.D: Provide compassionate, non-judgmental emergency care and stabilization

explanation: As nurses, our first oath is patient safety. We always provide life-saving emergency care with a warm, non-judgmental heart.

question: Why is it important for Nigerian nurses to understand local laws regarding abortion?

options.A: To arrest patients who attempt self-managed medication abortions at home
options.B: To prescribe mifepristone and misoprostol independently without a doctor's order
options.C: To navigate the restrictive laws while maintaining professional accountability and patient safety
options.D: To bypass hospital ethics committees during routine surgical procedures

explanation: Knowing the legal framework helps us stay safely within our nursing scope of practice while making sure our patients get the emergency help they need.

question: What kind of drug is misoprostol?

options.A: A selective progesterone receptor modulator
options.B: A synthetic prostaglandin E1 analogue
options.C: A long-acting synthetic estrogen derivative
options.D: A beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist

explanation: Misoprostol is made to copy prostaglandin E1, which naturally helps the cervix soften and triggers uterine contractions. You've got this!

question: Why is using misoprostol by itself very common in areas with limited healthcare resources?

options.A: It is widely available, affordable, and effective on its own
options.B: It completely prevents all normal cramping and heavy bleeding
options.C: It removes the need for any follow-up care
options.D: It works twice as fast as other drug combos

explanation: Because mifepristone is hard to get in many places, using misoprostol alone provides a practical and accessible option for safe care. Great job!

question: What are the two main ways misoprostol affects the uterus and cervix?

options.A: Decreasing blood flow and acting as local anesthesia
options.B: Stimulating contractions and causing cervical ripening
options.C: Blocking progesterone and shrinking the placenta
options.D: Paralyzing the muscle and closing the cervix tightly

explanation: Think of it as doing a two-step job: it softens the cervix so tissue can pass, and it helps the uterine muscle contract to push things out.

question: How do uterine contractions help during a medical abortion?

options.A: They push the gestational sac down and out through the dilated cervix
options.B: They raise blood pressure to flush out toxins
options.C: They permanently numb pelvic nerves so there is zero pain
options.D: They seal off the uterine lining to stop hormones

explanation: Once the cervix is soft, those rhythmic uterine contractions create the gentle pressure needed to clear the pregnancy tissue safely.

question: Which condition means a patient must NEVER be given misoprostol?

options.A: Well-managed gestational diabetes
options.B: Mild iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: A history of high blood pressure
options.D: A confirmed ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Misoprostol cannot treat a pregnancy outside the uterus. Giving it would dangerously delay emergency surgery. Always check for this first!

question: A patient wanting a medical abortion has an IUD in place. What should the nurse make sure happens first?

options.A: Ensure the IUD is removed prior to starting the misoprostol regimen
options.B: Leave the IUD in because misoprostol will push it out
options.C: Give extra antibiotics to stop local infections
options.D: Switch the patient immediately to vacuum aspiration

explanation: We need to take out any IUD before starting treatment to prevent serious infections or heavy bleeding. Simple and important safety step!

question: Which way of taking misoprostol gets into the bloodstream the fastest?

options.A: Vaginal
options.B: Oral
options.C: Rectal
options.D: Sublingual

explanation: Placing the pills under the tongue (sublingual) lets them absorb super fast into the blood vessels right there in the mouth. Brilliant shortcut!

question: What is a great benefit of using the vaginal route for misoprostol?

options.A: It works instantly in under five minutes
options.B: It means you don't need to know how far along the pregnancy is
options.C: It completely stops all cramping pain
options.D: It results in fewer gastrointestinal side effects like nausea

explanation: Vaginal use skips the stomach processing, which helps many patients avoid nasty stomach upset and vomiting. Smart clinical choice!

question: Why is an ultrasound or accurate dating so important before giving misoprostol?

options.A: To measure the pelvic muscles for pushing
options.B: To check the patient's exact blood type
options.C: To calculate the exact hospital bill
options.D: To rule out an ectopic pregnancy and verify gestational age

explanation: We always double-check that the pregnancy is inside the uterus and within safe limits before starting. Patient safety comes first!

question: What important advice should a nurse give a patient using the misoprostol-only method?

options.A: It has a 100 percent success rate on the first try
options.B: It requires staying in the hospital for three days
options.C: It has a higher rate of incomplete abortion than combination regimens
options.D: It never causes any physical discomfort

explanation: Being honest helps patients know that a follow-up visit might be needed since misoprostol alone isn't quite as strong as combination drugs.

question: What causes a mild fever and chills shortly after taking misoprostol?

options.A: A sudden drop in body temperature from blood loss
options.B: An allergic reaction to the pill ingredients
options.C: A severe bacterial bloodstream infection
options.D: The normal systemic pharmacologic action of prostaglandins

explanation: Prostaglandins can tweak the body's thermostat briefly, causing temporary chills and low fever that go away on their own. Nothing to panic about!

question: A patient calls 4 hours after taking misoprostol saying they have strong cramps, heavy bleeding with small clots, and mild nausea. What do you tell them?

options.A: Tell them to take a double dose of pills
options.B: Send them straight to the ER for a blood transfusion
options.C: Schedule emergency surgery for a hemorrhage
options.D: Tell the patient these are expected signs that the medication is working

explanation: Cramping and bleeding mean the drug is doing its job! Reassuring the patient builds trust and reduces panic.

question: Which symptom means a patient might be bleeding too much and needs urgent help?

options.A: Spotting light pink discharge for two weeks
options.B: Passing just one blood clot the size of a coin
options.C: Soaking two heavy pads per hour for two consecutive hours
options.D: Having mild cramping that gets better with rest

explanation: Soaking two big pads every hour for two hours straight is our red-flag sign for heavy bleeding that needs immediate medical review.

question: Which sign strongly points to a uterine infection instead of normal side effects?

options.A: Nausea that goes away in a day
options.B: Chills lasting only for the first two hours
options.C: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge and persistent fever
options.D: Cramping that feels worse than a normal period

explanation: Bad-smelling discharge and a fever that sticks around past day one are classic warning signs of infection like endometritis. Good to spot early!

question: When can a patient get pregnant again after a misoprostol medical abortion?

options.A: After six months for the uterus to heal
options.B: Never, because medical abortion causes permanent sterility
options.C: Immediately, as ovulation can resume before the next period
options.D: Only after waiting three normal menstrual cycles

explanation: Fertility bounces back super fast! Ovulation can happen even before the very first post-abortion period arrives.

question: Why is it important to talk about birth control before the patient leaves the clinic?

options.A: To make sure the hospital gets paid by insurance
options.B: To prevent unwanted repeat pregnancies given the rapid return of ovulation
options.C: To push the patient into long-term hormone use
options.D: To make sure the abortion pills keep working

explanation: Since fertility returns so quickly, offering birth control right away protects our patients from unplanned repeat pregnancies. Excellent nursing care!

question: What causes standard cramping pain after an abortion?

options.A: Buildup of gas inalos the large intestine
options.B: Contractions of the uterine muscle
options.C: Stretching of the abdominal wall skin
options.D: Infection of the urinary bladder

explanation: You've got this! The uterus naturally squeezes to return to its normal size after a procedure, and those muscular contractions cause period-like cramps. Totally normal part of healing!

question: Why do patients often feel sharp pressure in the lower belly right after an abortion?

options.A: Mechanical stretching and manipulation of the cervix
options.B: Swelling of the kidneys from retained fluid
options.C: Complete blockage of the Fallopian tubes
options.D: Rapid drop in systemic blood pressure levels

explanation: Opening the cervix during the procedure stretches local tissues, which leads to some sharp pressure or cramping right after. Great clinical insight to keep in mind!

question: What is a key sign that a post-abortion patient might be in severe pain?

options.A: Drop in body temperature below normal
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin sclera
options.C: Increased heart rate and breathing rate
options.D: Sudden swelling of the lower extremities

explanation: When someone is in acute pain, their body's natural fight-or-flight response kicks in, causing their heart rate and breathing to speed up. Brilliant nursing observation!

question: A nurse gives a patient pain medication. What is the best next step?

options.A: Instructing the patient to stop pressing the call bell
options.B: Documenting that the pain is completely gone forever
options.C: Reassessing the patient's pain level after a short interval
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately to save hospital beds

explanation: Always close the loop! Checking back in lets you know if the drug is actually doing its job or if the patient needs extra help.

question: Which type of medication is usually the first choice for treating post-abortion cramps?

options.A: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
options.B: Broad-spectrum oral antibiotics
options.C: Strong narcotic opioid analgesics
options.D: Central nervous system stimulants

explanation: NSAIDs like ibuprofen block prostaglandins, making them absolute superstars for tackling uterine cramps. Well done!

question: Why are strong opioid painkillers usually avoided for routine home care after an abortion?

options.A: They carry high risks of sedation, nausea, and dependency
options.B: They permanently damage the lining of the stomach
options.C: They cause the uterus to stop contracting completely
options.D: They raise blood pressure to dangerously high levels

explanation: Routine cramps can usually be handled safely with milder drugs, sparing the patient from heavy side effects like sleepiness and nausea. Makes total sense!

question: How does putting a heating pad on the lower belly help with post-abortion cramps?

options.A: It stops all vaginal bleeding instantly
options.B: It numbs the skin nerves permanently
options.C: It relaxes the uterine and pelvic muscles
options.D: It lowers the body temperature safely

explanation: Warmth boosts blood flow and helps tense muscles unwind, taking the sharp edge off those cramps. Simple and effective nursing comfort care!

question: What is a major plus of using comfort measures (like heat or rest) alongside medicines?

options.A: They guarantee the patient will have zero bleeding
options.B: They help reduce the overall need for heavy pain medications
options.C: They completely eliminate the need for any vital sign checks
options.D: They cure underlying infections without antibiotics

explanation: Combining simple comfort tricks with meds gives wonderful relief while keeping heavy drug use to a minimum. You're thinking like a holistic nurse!

question: Which symptom suggests a patient's pain is from retained tissue rather than normal recovery?

options.A: Temporary loss of appetite for a few hours
options.B: Mild lower back ache that goes away with rest
options.C: Itchy skin rash on the arms and chest
options.D: Severe cramping accompanied by heavy bleeding or large clots

explanation: If tissue is left behind, the uterus squeezes extra hard to push it out, causing intense cramps and heavy bleeding. Always watch out for this red flag!

question: Which of these is NOT a normal sign of post-abortion recovery?

options.A: Mild intermittent cramping similar to menstrual periods
options.B: Severe lower abdominal pain that worsens over time
options.C: Light spotting that gradually decreases over days
options.D: Occasional mild fatigue following the procedure

explanation: Pain that keeps getting worse instead of better is a warning sign that something needs medical attention. Great job spotting the abnormal finding!

question: Why should a nurse give written discharge instructions about pain meds to a recovering patient?

options.A: It replaces the need for any verbal conversation entirely
options.B: Written papers are legally required to keep nurses from being sued
options.C: Patients often forget verbal instructions due to stress and fatigue
options.D: Pharmacies will not sell pain medication without hospital paper

explanation: When people are stressed or tired, details slip their minds. Written guides are lifesavers for safe home care!

question: A patient getting ready for discharge is worried about taking her pain pills right. What should you do first?

options.A: Tell the patient not to worry because pain is all in the mind
options.B: Cancel the prescription and give only herbal remedies instead
options.C: Ask a family member to manage all medication doses at home
options.D: Review the medication schedule slowly and check for understanding

explanation: Taking a little extra time to walk through the dosing schedule ensures the patient feels confident and safe at home. Excellent patient advocacy!

question: How soon can ovulation return after an abortion procedure?

options.A: Only when the first normal period ends
options.B: After 6 months have passed
options.C: Within 10 to 14 days
options.D: After exactly 4 to 6 weeks

explanation: Ovulation often resumes very quickly after pregnancy termination, sometimes within two weeks, meaning a new pregnancy is possible before normal menstruation returns. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h1)

question: What is the main risk of delaying contraceptive counseling until the first post-procedure menstrual period?

options.A: An increased risk of an unintended repeat pregnancy
options.B: Immediate surgical complications from the abortion
options.C: Total loss of hormonal control in the body
options.D: Permanent damage to the ovarian lining

explanation: Because ovulation happens before the first period, waiting until menstruation returns leaves the client unprotected during the fertile window. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h1)

question: What does client-centered contraceptive counseling prioritize above all else?

options.A: The personal reproductive goals and choices of the client
options.B: The hospital policy on family planning targets
options.C: The nurse's personal preference for birth control methods
options.D: The fastest and cheapest method available in the clinic

explanation: Client-centered care centers entirely on the individual's needs, preferences, and life circumstances rather than outside pressures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h2)

question: Why must a nurse review a client's medical history before recommending a hormonal contraceptive?

options.A: To check if the client has ever had a routine dental cleaning
options.B: To determine how many children the client currently has at home
options.C: To screen for conditions that could make specific methods unsafe
options.D: To calculate the exact cost of the prescription for the pharmacy

explanation: Certain medical conditions, such as high blood pressure or blood clotting disorders, make specific hormonal methods dangerous to use. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h2)

question: What does immediate contraceptive initiation mean in post-abortion care?

options.A: Starting pills only when the client feels severe pelvic pain
options.B: Starting the method before the client leaves the clinic after the procedure
options.C: Waiting for three normal menstrual cycles before starting any method
options.D: Using barrier methods only after the follow-up appointment next month

explanation: Immediate initiation provides protection right away while the client is still at the healthcare facility, reducing the risk of an unremembered follow-up. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h3)

question: A client is discharged after an abortion without a birth control method and fails to return for her two-week checkup. What major risk does she face?

options.A: A permanent inability to ever produce estrogen again
options.B: An unintended repeat pregnancy due to early ovulation
options.C: Severe weight loss from sudden hormonal withdrawal
options.D: An automatic infection in the uterine lining

explanation: Missing the follow-up without a started method leaves a gap in protection during a time when fertility has already returned. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h3)

question: Which of the following is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive method?

options.A: A subdermal hormonal implant
options.B: A packet of daily oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Spermicidal foam applied before sex
options.D: Male latex condoms used during intercourse

explanation: Implants and intrauterine devices are classified as LARC methods because they work continuously for years without daily action from the user. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h4)

question: Why are LARC methods considered very effective for post-abortion contraception?

options.A: They completely stop all bacteria from entering the reproductive tract
options.B: They do not require daily action or memory from the user to prevent pregnancy
options.C: They destroy all male sperm cells before they reach the vagina
options.D: They can only be removed permanently by surgical removal of the uterus

explanation: Human error, like forgetting a pill, is a major cause of contraceptive failure, which LARC methods bypass entirely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h4)

question: What is a major clinical advantage of barrier methods compared to hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: They provide protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.B: They guarantee a 100 percent prevention rate against pregnancy
options.C: They alter the body's natural hormone levels permanently
options.D: They last for five continuous years without replacement

explanation: Condoms and other barriers block physical contact and infectious fluids, something hormonal birth control cannot do. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h5)

question: Which factor most often decreases the effectiveness of short-acting hormonal methods like oral contraceptive pills?

options.A: Inconsistent daily use or missed doses by the client
options.B: The time of day the client eats her meals
options.C: The client's natural blood pressure levels
options.D: Using the pills during the winter months

explanation: Short-acting methods depend heavily on the user remembering to take or apply them on a strict schedule every day. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h5)

question: How should a nurse respond when a client expresses fear that an IUD will cause permanent infertility?

options.A: Tell the client that her fears are irrational and insist she accepts the device anyway
options.B: Provide calm, evidence-based education explaining that fertility returns immediately upon IUD removal
options.C: Agree that permanent damage is common and suggest she avoids all birth control
options.D: Ignore the comment and document that the client refused all medical advice

explanation: Respectful nursing care involves correcting myths gently with factual information while supporting the client's ultimate autonomy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a true fact about modern post-abortion contraceptive use?

options.A: Ovulation returns within two weeks for many women after an abortion
options.B: Barrier methods protect against common sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Contraceptives cause permanent damage to a woman's reproductive organs
options.D: Intrauterine devices can be inserted safely right after a procedure

explanation: Standard reversible contraceptives do not cause permanent organ damage; fertility recovers once the method is stopped or removed. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h6)

question: What critical warning signs should a nurse teach a post-abortion client before she leaves the clinic?

options.A: Slight breast tenderness in the morning
options.B: Severe pelvic pain, heavy bleeding, or high fever
options.C: A temporary change in her favorite foods
options.D: Mild fatigue and slight spotting for two days

explanation: These symptoms are red flags that can indicate infection, retained tissue, or other complications requiring immediate medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h7)

question: Why is proper documentation of contraceptive counseling important in the client's health record?

options.A: It stops the client from ever changing her birth control method later
options.B: It proves to the hospital management that the nurse worked full hours
options.C: It guarantees that the healthcare facility will receive extra government funding
options.D: It ensures continuity of care and creates a legal record of the client's informed choices

explanation: Clear records allow other healthcare providers to know what method was chosen, what education was given, and what follow-up is needed. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h7)

question: What is the main goal of offering family planning right after an abortion?

options.A: To delay physical healing after pregnancy loss
options.B: To check for lower abdominal infections
options.C: To stop pregnancy from ever happening again
options.D: To help prevent rapid, unplanned repeat pregnancies

explanation: Offering contraception right away helps patients protect their bodies and avoid another unplanned pregnancy before they feel ready. You've got this!

question: Why is it so important to talk about family planning right after an abortion?

options.A: Patients lose natural immunity without hormonal birth control
options.B: Hormonal pills speed up physical recovery from a miscarriage
options.C: Fertility returns very quickly after an abortion procedure
options.D: Patients are required by law to start birth control immediately

explanation: Ovulation can happen as early as two weeks after an abortion! That means a patient can get pregnant again before their next period even arrives.

question: How soon can a patient start ovulating again after an abortion?

options.A: Only after three normal monthly cycles
options.B: After exactly six months
options.C: As early as 10 to 14 days
options.D: Once the patient reaches menopause

explanation: The ovaries can release an egg just two weeks post-abortion, even before bleeding stops. Good to keep in mind for patient education!

question: A patient asks if she can get pregnant before her first period returns after an abortion. What should you tell her?

options.A: No, menstruation must happen first to clear the path
options.B: No, the body is completely sterile for three months
options.C: Yes, because ovulation happens before the first period returns
options.D: Only if she had a surgical procedure instead of a medical one

explanation: Many patients are surprised by this! Ovulation happens first, meaning pregnancy is possible before that first post-abortion period shows up.

question: What is the main benefit of using a person-centred approach in post-abortion counseling?

options.A: It helps match birth control to the client's unique lifestyle and goals
options.B: It guarantees the patient will never feel any grief
options.C: It speeds up the clinic discharge paperwork
options.D: It forces the client to choose the strongest long-term method

explanation: Person-centred care is all about listening to what the patient wants. When they choose a method that fits their life, they are much happier using it!

question: Which attitude is most important for a nurse during post-abortion counseling?

options.A: Non-judgmental and empathetic
options.B: Skeptical and questioning
options.C: Indifferent and detached
options.D: Strictly authoritative and firm

explanation: Being warm, kind, and non-judgmental builds trust, making the patient feel safe to share their worries and ask questions.

question: Which type of birth control protects against both unplanned pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Hormonal injections
options.B: Intrauterine devices (IUDs)
options.C: Long-acting implants
options.D: Barrier methods

explanation: Condoms and other barrier methods act as a physical shield against both sperm and infections. Simple and effective!

question: A patient wants an IUD right after an uncomplicated surgical abortion. What is the standard clinical practice?

options.A: She must wait for two normal menstrual periods
options.B: It can be safely inserted right away if there is no sign of infection
options.C: IUDs are never recommended after pregnancy termination
options.D: She must wait six weeks for her uterus to shrink

explanation: As long as there's no infection or trauma, an IUD can be placed immediately after the procedure. Saves the patient an extra trip!

question: When is the best time to start a chosen birth control method after an abortion?

options.A: Only after the six-week follow-up visit
options.B: On the exact same day as the abortion procedure
options.C: After waiting for three complete menstrual cycles
options.D: When cervical mucus changes appear

explanation: Starting contraception on day one ensures the patient is protected before ovulation sneaks up on them.

question: What is the main risk of waiting until a six-week check-up to start birth control?

options.A: The patient may experience an unplanned pregnancy before the visit
options.B: The body will reject hormonal methods after six weeks
options.C: The patient's natural hormone levels will drop permanently
options.D: It becomes illegal to prescribe birth control then

explanation: Since ovulation can return in just two weeks, waiting six weeks leaves a huge window for another unintended pregnancy.

question: A patient refuses birth control pills because she heard they cause permanent infertility. How should you reply?

options.A: Ignore her concern and write the prescription anyway
options.B: Explain that fertility returns quickly once pills are stopped
options.C: Tell her infertility is the price for effective protection
options.D: Agree with her and suggest only natural calendar tracking

explanation: Clearing up this myth reassures the patient that her body will be ready to conceive in the future whenever she chooses.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier stopping women from using post-abortion contraception?

options.A: Fear of unpleasant side effects
options.B: Lack of transport to the clinic
options.C: Guaranteed 100 percent long-term effectiveness
options.D: High product costs at the pharmacy

explanation: High effectiveness is a great thing! Fear, cost, and travel issues are the real hurdles patients face.

question: A patient calls two days after an abortion saying she is soaking through three large pads every hour. What should you tell her?

options.A: Reassure her that heavy bleeding lasts a whole month
options.B: Tell her it is normal and to call back next week
options.C: Take extra birth control pills to slow down the flow
options.D: Come to the clinic or emergency department right away

explanation: Soaking more than two pads an hour for two hours is a major red flag for heavy bleeding. She needs medical attention urgently!

question: Why do we schedule a follow-up visit a few weeks after starting post-abortion family planning?

options.A: To run routine blood tests for hidden diseases
options.B: To close her medical file and discharge her forever
options.C: To force the patient to buy a more expensive brand
options.D: To check physical healing and see if her birth control method suits her

explanation: Follow-ups let us confirm she is healing nicely and make sure her birth control method is working comfortably for her lifestyle.

question: When giving nursing care after an abortion, what does a holistic approach mainly mean?

options.A: Recognizing overlapping systemic illnesses
options.B: Treating only physical symptoms
options.C: Focusing solely on uterine health
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately

explanation: Great nursing looks at the whole person! Comprehensive care means looking beyond just the reproductive system to see how other health conditions might affect the patient's recovery.

question: Why is keeping an eye on chronic health conditions so important during post-abortion care?

options.A: It guarantees immediate fertility restoration
options.B: It prevents minor issues from becoming emergencies
options.C: It eliminates the need for pain medication
options.D: It reduces hospital administrative costs

explanation: Spotting and managing chronic diseases early stops them from flaring up and getting worse during a time when the body is under physical stress.

question: During the first assessment, why do nurses do medication reconciliation?

options.A: To avoid dangerous drug interactions
options.B: To prescribe new vitamins
options.C: To reduce the cost of hospital drugs
options.D: To test the patient's memory

explanation: Checking all the drugs and supplements a patient is already taking helps you make sure new medications won't mix badly with them.

question: A patient with a history of asthma is admitted for post-abortion care. What is your most important first step?

options.A: Discharging the patient with an inhaler
options.B: Starting intravenous antibiotic therapy
options.C: Establishing accurate baseline vital signs
options.D: Restricting all oral fluids immediately

explanation: Getting accurate baseline vitals gives you a starting point so you can quickly spot any sudden changes in breathing or circulation.

question: Why do patients with diabetes need frequent blood sugar checks after an abortion?

options.A: Insulin is no longer effective after surgery
options.B: Physical stress and hormonal shifts cause rapid sugar changes
options.C: Abortion procedures automatically cure diabetes
options.D: Blood sugar levels always drop to zero

explanation: Physical stress and changing hormones make blood sugar levels bounce around, making them much harder to control during recovery.

question: In patients with high blood pressure, what common recovery factor can trigger a dangerous blood pressure spike?

options.A: Pain and anxiety
options.B: Sleeping on the left side
options.C: Eating fresh vegetables
options.D: Drinking too much water

explanation: When a patient feels pain or emotional stress, their nervous system kicks in, which can cause their blood pressure to shoot up.

question: Why are patients with weak immune systems at much higher risk after an abortion procedure?

options.A: They are allergic to all surgical instruments
options.B: They absorb pain medications much faster than other patients
options.C: Their bodies cannot produce red blood cells
options.D: Their weakened defenses allow normal flora to cause severe infection

explanation: When the immune system is down, it struggles to fight off everyday bacteria that normally wouldn't cause any trouble.

question: Which of these is NOT a good nursing practice when caring for a post-abortion patient with a weak immune system?

options.A: Maintaining strict aseptic techniques
options.B: Administering prescribed prophylactic antibiotics
options.C: Skipping hand hygiene between patients
options.D: Monitoring for subtle temperature spikes

explanation: Never skip hand hygiene! Clean hands are always a must, especially when caring for vulnerable patients who can easily catch infections.

question: How can hormonal shifts and physical stress impact a patient who already has a mental health condition?

options.A: They can significantly worsen existing psychiatric disorders
options.B: They permanently cure depression and anxiety
options.C: They have no impact on emotional well-being
options.D: They only affect physical organ function

explanation: Recovering from physical stress combined with sudden hormone changes can easily trigger or intensify existing mental health challenges.

question: What is the best first step when you are caring for a distressed patient who has a history of anxiety?

options.A: Isolating the patient in a dark room alone
options.B: Creating a calm and non-judgmental environment
options.C: Ignoring the emotional symptoms completely
options.D: Telling the patient to stop worrying immediately

explanation: A safe, supportive atmosphere helps soothe the patient's nerves, lowers their anxiety, and makes it easier for them to talk to you.

question: Who acts as the central link for coordinating care between the patient and various medical specialists?

options.A: The nurse
options.B: The patient's family
options.C: The hospital accountant
options.D: The pharmacist

explanation: As the nurse, you are the heartbeat of the ward! You coordinate the care plan and make sure information flows smoothly between everyone involved.

question: A post-abortion patient suddenly develops severe chest pain and shortness of breath on the ward. What should you do right away?

options.A: Waiting until the end of the shift to report the finding
options.B: Discharging the patient home for rest
options.C: Requesting immediate consultation with the appropriate medical specialist
options.D: Telling the patient that chest pain is normal after an abortion

explanation: Chest pain and trouble breathing are red flags. Unstable symptoms like these mean you need to call for a specialist review right away.

question: Why must nurses carefully check a patient's medical history before recommending hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: Contraceptives only work if the patient has high blood pressure
options.B: Hormones prevent the absorption of regular food
options.C: Some methods are dangerous for patients with blood clots or liver disease
options.D: All birth control methods cure chronic illnesses

explanation: Certain hormones can cause serious complications if a patient already has issues like clotting disorders or liver trouble.

question: A patient with a history of severe blood clots asks for birth control after an abortion. Which method should you avoid?

options.A: Progestin-only injections
options.B: Copper intrauterine devices
options.C: Combined oral contraceptive pills
options.D: Male and female barrier condoms

explanation: Combined pills contain estrogen, which increases the risk of dangerous blood clots in patients who are already vulnerable to them.

question: What is a primary public health consequence of unintended pregnancy in Nigeria?

options.A: Decreased overall population growth
options.B: Elevated maternal morbidity and mortality
options.C: Immediate reduction in rural poverty
options.D: Eradication of infectious childhood diseases

explanation: Unintended pregnancies often lead to unsafe practices or lack of timely antenatal care, directly driving up rates of maternal illness and death. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h1)

question: Why must interventions for unintended pregnancy extend beyond traditional hospital walls?

options.A: Hospitals are exclusively reserved for surgical emergencies
options.B: Community spaces allow nurses to reach individuals before they experience a crisis
options.C: Government policy prohibits clinics from distributing contraceptives
options.D: Physicians refuse to discuss family planning inside clinical settings

explanation: Taking education and services directly into neighborhoods helps overcome physical and financial barriers to clinic attendance. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h1)

question: What does equity ensure within community-based reproductive health initiatives?

options.A: Fair access to dialogue and services for marginalized groups
options.B: Identical healthcare facilities in every state of the country
options.C: Equal financial compensation for all community leaders
options.D: Universal free distribution of all surgical procedures

explanation: Equity focuses on bridging gaps so vulnerable populations, such as adolescents and rural poor, receive necessary health support. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h2)

question: Why is local capacity building considered essential for sustainable community health projects?

options.A: It allows foreign organizations to permanently withdraw from the region
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future government healthcare budgets
options.C: It prevents community members from seeking care at tertiary hospitals
options.D: It ensures health programs continue functioning after external funding stops

explanation: When local leaders and volunteers are trained to manage programs, the initiative survives even when initial project lifecycles conclude. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h2)

question: Who are considered key gatekeepers in many Nigerian community settings?

options.A: Traditional rulers and religious clerics
options.B: International pharmaceutical manufacturers
options.C: Federal immigration enforcement officers
options.D: Primary school students and young children

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders hold significant social influence and must be consulted to gain trust and entry into local communities. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h3)

question: Which demographic group often faces the highest social barriers when accessing contraceptive information?

options.A: Wealthy urban entrepreneurs
options.B: Married middle-aged civil servants
options.C: Elderly retired community chiefs
options.D: Adolescents and young unmarried women

explanation: Societal stigma and cultural expectations often penalize youth who seek reproductive health services, making them highly vulnerable. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h3)

question: What is the primary advantage of utilizing mobile health outreaches in rural areas?

options.A: They permanently replace the need for general hospitals
options.B: They bring screening and contraceptives directly to remote populations
options.C: They operate entirely without the need for trained nurses
options.D: They eliminate all cultural beliefs regarding family planning

explanation: Mobile outreaches overcome geographic isolation by delivering care physically closer to those who cannot easily travel to a clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h4)

question: Why is peer education particularly effective when targeting adolescents for reproductive health?

options.A: Peers hold official medical licenses to prescribe oral medications
options.B: Adolescents refuse to listen to anyone over the age of twenty
options.C: Peers share similar social contexts and language, reducing intimidation
options.D: Peer educators are the only individuals who understand contraceptive biology

explanation: Young people often feel more comfortable discussing sensitive topics like sexuality and contraception with someone of their own age group. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h4)

question: A patient expresses fear that using modern contraceptives will cause permanent sterility. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Dismiss the concern and insist on immediate insertion of an IUD
options.B: Scold the patient for believing unscientific rumors
options.C: Refer the patient directly to a psychiatric hospital
options.D: Listen empathetically and provide clear, factual education

explanation: Validating fears and calmly offering accurate information builds trust and corrects misconceptions without shaming the client. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical myth associated with modern contraceptives in many communities?

options.A: They protect against chronic waterborne infections
options.B: They cause permanent infertility
options.C: They promote general promiscuity
options.D: They lead to physical deformity

explanation: Contraceptives prevent pregnancy and some prevent STIs, but protecting against waterborne infections like typhoid or cholera is entirely unrelated. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h5)

question: What primary position do nurse-midwives occupy in the healthcare delivery system?

options.A: The vital bridge between formal health systems and grassroots populations
options.B: Strictly inpatient surgical assistants in tertiary centers
options.C: Independent pharmaceutical manufacturers and suppliers
options.D: Exclusive administrative managers in federal ministries

explanation: Nurse-midwives work directly within communities and primary centers, connecting local residents to professional healthcare resources. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h6)

question: A nurse working in a rural primary health center wants to improve youth turnout for family planning education. What is the best strategy?

options.A: Post warning notices about unintended pregnancy on community bulletin boards
options.B: Wait quietly inside the clinic office for youth to arrive independently
options.C: Collaborate with local schools and youth groups to establish friendly outreach sessions
options.D: Report uncooperative youth to local law enforcement authorities

explanation: Proactive collaboration creates safe, welcoming environments that encourage young people to seek health information. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring and evaluation in community health programs?

options.A: To track progress indicators and ensure programs achieve their objectives
options.B: To permanently increase the cost of healthcare services
options.C: To punish staff members who fail to meet strict quotas
options.D: To eliminate the need for community stakeholder meetings

explanation: Monitoring and evaluation provide data on what is working well and where adjustments are needed to meet public health goals. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h7)

question: Why are regular feedback meetings with community stakeholders critical for long-term project success?

options.A: They legally bind community leaders to fund the national health budget
options.B: They allow the program to adapt to changing local needs and maintain local support
options.C: They guarantee that all health services will become completely free
options.D: They prevent external organizations from ever leaving the region
